questions.question: On a two-way road, where must you drive?

options.text: Always in the middle of the road

questions.explanation: In South Africa, vehicles must always drive on the left-hand side of a two-way road. This keeps traffic organized and prevents head-on collisions.

questions.question: What is considered the most important rule of the road?

options.text: Always keep left and pass right
Always drive below the speed limit

questions.explanation: The most important rule of the road ensures smooth traffic flow. Keeping left allows faster-moving vehicles to overtake safely from the right, reducing congestion and accidents.

questions.question: When are you allowed to drive on the right-hand side of the road?

options.text: When driving on a one-way road

questions.explanation: One-way roads are designed for vehicles to travel in a single direction. If no signs indicate otherwise, you may drive on the right-hand side of a one-way street.

questions.question: What is the recommended following distance for a light motor vehicle?
questions.explanation: A 2-second following distance gives light motor vehicles enough time to react if the vehicle ahead suddenly stops. This reduces the risk of rear-end collisions.

questions.question: What is the recommended following distance for a heavy motor vehicle?
questions.explanation: Heavy vehicles take longer to stop due to their weight. A 3-second gap provides extra braking time, especially at higher speeds or on wet roads.

questions.question: What must always be displayed on a vehicle?
questions.explanation: A vehicle's licence disc proves it is legally registered and roadworthy. It must always be displayed on the windscreen for law enforcement to check.

questions.question: How long is a vehicle's licence disc valid for?
questions.explanation: Vehicle licence discs in South Africa must be renewed annually to ensure that vehicles on the road remain legally registered and roadworthy.

questions.question: If a traffic officer gives you an instruction that contradicts a road rule, what should you do?

options.text: Ignore the officer and follow road rules

questions.explanation: A traffic officer's instructions override road rules or signs because they manage traffic in real-time to ensure safety, especially in emergencies or roadblocks.

questions.question: On a divided road (with a painted line or barrier), where must you drive?

options.text: In the middle of the road

questions.explanation: Divided roads separate opposing traffic. Driving on the left ensures orderly traffic flow and reduces the risk of head-on collisions.

questions.question: When may you cross a painted line or barrier dividing the road?

options.text: Only at an indicated opening or space
At any point where the road is clear

questions.explanation: Divisions exist to separate lanes safely. Crossing them at unauthorized points can lead to accidents or traffic violations.

questions.question: When is it acceptable to drive continuously on the shoulder of the road?

options.text: When no other vehicles are present

questions.explanation: The road shoulder is for emergencies, breakdowns, or pedestrian use. Driving on it continuously is unsafe and illegal.

questions.question: Under what conditions may you temporarily drive on the shoulder to let another vehicle overtake?

options.text: Only if you can see at least 150 meters ahead and there are no obstacles
At any time to allow faster cars to pass

questions.explanation: Temporarily moving onto the shoulder can help with overtaking, but only if it is safe, with a clear view of the road ahead.

questions.question: When is it legal to drive on the shoulder to allow overtaking?

options.text: At night, when the road is empty
Only on a single-lane road and during daylight hours

questions.explanation: Driving on the shoulder is only allowed under controlled conditions (during daylight and on single-lane roads) to ensure safety and visibility.
